costGuide.title: Mercedes-Benz M166 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an M166 engine typically takes 8-12 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for this engine is the condition of the crankshaft position sensor (CPS), the ignition coil pack, and the valve cover gasket. Because the M166 is mounted at a steep 70-degree angle, recon specialists will typically replace all hardened rubber seals, fit a new CPS, and upgrade the coil pack assembly as standard to prevent immediate post-installation failures. failures.title: Mercedes-Benz M166 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor (CPS) Failure
items.whatHappens: The CPS is exposed to heat cycles and its internal wiring can degrade over time. This causes the sensor to fail when the engine is hot, resulting in sudden stalling, a no-start condition, or rough running until the engine cools down.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the CPS is a relatively inexpensive and straightforward repair. It is highly recommended to replace the sensor proactively during any major engine service.

items.title: Ignition Coil Pack Degradation
items.whatHappens: The M166 uses a single, integrated ignition coil pack with attached wiring leads. Over time, the plastic housing can crack, or the internal windings can fail, leading to misfires, rough idling, and poor acceleration.
items.repairVsReplace: The entire coil pack assembly must be replaced as a single unit. Upgrading to a high-quality OEM-spec coil pack resolves the issue permanently.

items.title: Oil Leaks (Valve Cover & Oil Filter Housing)
items.whatHappens: The rubber gaskets for the valve cover and oil filter housing harden and shrink with age and heat cycles. Due to the engine's angled mounting, oil can pool in specific areas, exacerbating leaks and creating burning oil smells.
items.repairVsReplace: These are routine maintenance items. Replacing the gaskets is relatively inexpensive in terms of parts, though the angled layout requires careful access.

failures.goodYearsLine: The M166 is widely regarded as a simple, robust, and reliable engine. Its SOHC 8-valve design lacks the complexity of modern multi-valve engines, and units maintained with regular oil changes routinely exceed 150,000 miles without major internal bottom-end issues .

variants.title: M166 Sub-Codes Explained - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: ═══════════════════════════════════════ INTRO: The M166 family shares the same fundamental SOHC 8-valve inline-4 block architecture and unique 70-degree angled mounting, but displacement varies significantly. Identifying your exact sub-code is mandatory, as fitting the wrong revision can lead to ECU and performance incompatibility. - Fitted to: A-Class W168 (A 140, A 160), Vaneo W414 (1.6) - Key technical difference: The entry-level variant, designed for maximum fuel economy and low running costs in urban environments. Features a shorter stroke and specific port fuel injection mapping. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; no unique widespread defects. - Interchange note: Not a straight swap with the 1.9L variant due to different ECU mapping, exhaust systems, and minor ancillary differences. - Fitted to: A-Class W168 (A 190), Vaneo W414 (1.9) - Key technical difference: The high-output variant, featuring a longer stroke, revised intake manifold, and a slightly higher compression ratio to deliver stronger mid-range torque and improved highway drivability. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; the higher continuous thermal loads can slightly accelerate valve cover gasket degradation. - Interchange note: Requires matching ECU calibration and exhaust components; not a direct drop-in for 1.6L chassis without modification.

relatives.description: the 1.5L-2.0L inline-4 that replaced the M166 in the W169 A-Class, introducing turbocharging and a more conventional mounting angle while retaining the pioneering sandwich floor safety concept.
the contemporary 1.8L inline-4 that shared a similar era of Mercedes compact engineering, though mounted longitudinally in the C-Class and CLK, featuring a timing chain and Kompressor options.

variants.closing: The engine code is stamped on the right-hand side of the cylinder block, near the oil filter housing. It will also be listed on your V5C logbook under "Engine Capacity" or visible via a VIN decode. Not sure? Enter your registration above for instant confirmation.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement M166 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used M166 engine makes sense only if it comes with verifiable service history and documented proof of a recent CPS and coil pack replacement. Given the age of these vehicles, buying a used unit with unknown history risks immediate, albeit minor, electrical or seal-related repairs.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned M166 engine is the sweet spot for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will proactively address the common failure points by fitting a new CPS, upgrading the coil pack assembly, and renewing all brittle valve cover and oil seals, giving the engine a fresh, reliable lease on life.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full M166 engine rebuild is highly justified for low-mileage or collector W168 A 190 models where originality, matching numbers, and maximum longevity are required. An upgraded rebuild should include line-boring the block, new pistons/rings, and a balanced crankshaft.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your M166 engine is installed by specialists familiar with the unique angled "sandwich floor" layout, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Because the M166 is typically found in W168 and W414 vehicles valued between £1,000 and £4,000 (with pristine A 190 models commanding slightly higher premiums), a full replacement can represent a significant portion of the vehicle's worth. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate the investment carefully .

items.question: How much does a Mercedes M166 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Mercedes M166 engine typically costs between £1,200 and £2,200 for supply only . Fitted costs generally range from £1,800 to £3,000 depending on the specialist, while used units can be found from £400 but carry a higher risk due to the engine's age and potential seal degradation. → Compare M166 engine replacement quotes today

items.question: What is the most common failure on the M166 engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are crankshaft position sensor (CPS) failure, ignition coil pack degradation, and oil leaks from the valve cover or oil filter housing. The CPS can cause sudden stalling when hot, while the integrated coil pack is prone to cracking and misfires over time. → Get quotes for a rebuilt M166 with these issues resolved

items.question: Which Mercedes models use the M166 engine?
items.answer: The M166 was fitted to the W168 A-Class (A 140, A 160, A 190) and the W414 Vaneo (1.6, 1.9), serving as the definitive compact petrol engine for these unique, space-efficient chassis between 1997 and 2005. → Check your registration to confirm your exact M166 fitment

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned M166 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned M166 is strongly recommended over a used unit. A proper rebuild will proactively address the common failure points of age by fitting a new CPS, upgrading the coil pack assembly, and renewing all brittle valve cover and oil seals, whereas a used engine with unknown history risks immediate, albeit minor, electrical or seal-related repairs. → Compare reconditioned M166 engine prices from UK specialists

items.question: What is the difference between M166.920 and M166.940?
items.answer: The M166.920 is the 1.6L entry-level variant producing 75-102 hp, designed for maximum fuel economy. The M166.940 is the 1.9L high-output variant producing 125 hp, featuring a longer stroke and revised intake manifold for stronger mid-range torque. They share the same core block and angled mounting, but require matching ECU calibration and exhaust components. → Enter your reg above to identify your exact M166 sub-code ═══════════════════════════════════════
